title: A lifted top residue cell with a complete cone of shorter amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_{n,T}=(R/\varpi^n)_T$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_{n,T}$, using constant sheaves and inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $M$ is quotient-tower complete if its canonical quotient maps exhibit it as $R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})$, with the quotient transitions and with the terms restricted to $B_T$-scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact and evaluation at $T$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ be quotient-tower complete and write $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T$. Fix integers $a\leq b$ and finite integers $r_q\geq0$ for $q\in[a,b]$, and choose isomorphisms $\theta_q:k_T^{\oplus r_q}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(M_1)$. Assume $M_1$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ after restriction to every site object, meaning $H^j((M_1|_V)\otimes^L_{k_V}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, every site object $V\to T$ and every degree-zero $k_V$-module sheaf $N$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Put $P=B_T^{\oplus r_b}$. There exist a morphism $f:P[-b]\to M$ and a distinguished triangle
$$P[-b]\xrightarrow{f}M\longrightarrow L\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1]$$
such that $L$ is quotient-tower complete and the reduction $f_1:k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to M_1$ induces the prescribed $\theta_b$. Under any zero-differential residue model inducing the $\theta_q$, the map $f_1$ is the top summand inclusion, and its cone has a model which is the direct sum of $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$ and the contractible identity complex on $k_T^{\oplus r_b}$ in degrees $b-1,b$. In particular
$$L\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T\cong\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q],$$
with constant finite-dimensional cohomology and Tor amplitude $[a,b-1]$ after restriction to every site object when $a<b$. If $a=b$ the residue cone and $L$ are zero and $f$ is an isomorphism. Rank $r_b=0$ is allowed, with $P=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-complete-residue-cohomology-bounds] to $M$: quasi-compactness, quotient-tower completeness and the stated residue Tor bound give $H^{b+1}(M)=0$. Apply the $n=1$ reduction triangle of [lem-sf-completed-coefficient-free-resolution] and its long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. The segment $H^b(M)\to H^b(\operatorname{Res}M_1)\to H^{b+1}(M)$ shows that the canonical reduction map $H^b(M)\to H^b(M_1)$, regarded in $B_T$-modules, is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tags 09C2 (lemma-describe-constructible-complexes), proof of (1)-(2), and 09C3 (lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex), final induction paragraph; long exact sequence: derived.tex Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological

proof.text: Evaluation at $T$ preserves homology by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact], under exactly the assumed epimorphism-surjectivity hypothesis; applying it to the epimorphism in step 1 makes the map on sections surjective. Lift each section $\theta_b(e_i)$ to $x_i\in H^b(M)(T)$. The shifted-free Hom bijection of [lem-sf-projective-cohomology-split-model], with $C=B_T$, gives $f:B_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]\to M$ with generator images $x_i$. After derived scalar extension each generator maps to the reduction of $x_i$, hence $H^b(f_1)(e_i)=\theta_b(e_i)$ and $H^b(f_1)=\theta_b$. If $r_b=0$, the tuple is empty and this is the unique map from zero.

proof.text: Complete $f$ to a distinguished triangle $P[-b]\to M\to L\to P[-b+1]$, using TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The source $P[-b]$ is quotient-tower complete by [lem-sf-completed-coefficient-free-resolution]. The canonical ring-sheaf identification $B_T\cong\mathcal O_{E,T}$ of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] identifies the actual quotient maps, their transitions and the completeness comparison with those of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: the maps to the constant finite quotients are the inverse-limit projections. Thus both source and target are complete in the convention of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]. Its closure-under-cones clause makes $L$ complete, and the same identification gives quotient-tower completeness of $L$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, triangle in the final induction paragraph; completeness: lemma-derived-complete-zero and derived completion section; the cited integral-limit identification fixes the coefficient convention

proof.text: Derived extension along $B_T\to k_T$ is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so the triangle in step 3 reduces to a distinguished triangle with third term $L_1=L\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T$. The single-term complex $P[-b]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]: its tensor with an acyclic complex is a finite sum of shifts of that complex. Thus its reduction is $k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]$, with its actual free generators. The Tor bound implies $H^q(M_1)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ by taking the test module $k_T$. Apply [lem-sf-projective-cohomology-split-model] with $C=k_T$, $N=M_1$, and the given $\theta_q$. It supplies the zero-differential model $V=\bigoplus_{q=a}^b k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$. Let $\varphi:V\xrightarrow{\sim}M_1$ be any isomorphism in the derived category inducing the $\theta_q$, and let $i$ be the top summand inclusion. Then $\varphi\circ i$ and $f_1$ both send the standard generators to $\theta_b(e_j)\in H^b(M_1)(T)$, so by the injectivity of the shifted-free Hom bijection of [lem-sf-projective-cohomology-split-model] (for $C=k_T$, $q=b$, $r=r_b$) $f_1=\varphi\circ i$: under every such model $f_1$ is exactly $i$.

proof.text: Put $A=k_T^{\oplus r_b}[-b]$ and $W=\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_T^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$. By the cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C(i)^j=V^j\oplus A^{j+1}$ and $d(v,x)=(i(x),0)$. Splitting $V=W\oplus A$ gives $C(i)=W\oplus D$, where $D$ has $k_T^{\oplus r_b}$ in degrees $b-1,b$ and differential the identity. On $D$ set $h^b=\mathrm{id}:D^b\to D^{b-1}$ and $h^j=0$ otherwise. In degrees $b-1$ and $b$, respectively, $hd=\mathrm{id}$ and $dh=\mathrm{id}$; hence $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}_D$. Projection to $W$ and its inclusion are inverse up to this homotopy and induce cohomology isomorphisms. Therefore $C(i)\cong W$ in the derived category. TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] extends the identity on $A$ and the chosen isomorphism $M_1\cong V$ to a morphism from the reduced triangle to the cone triangle of $i$. Its third map $L_1\to C(i)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. This proves the asserted cone model and $L_1\cong W$.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle; explicit identity-complex contraction expanding the details omitted in proetale.tex Tag 09C3

proof.text: For any site object $V'\to T$, the model $W|_{V'}$ is the finite sum $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}k_{V'}^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$ with zero differential. For an acyclic complex $F$, its total tensor with this model is a finite direct sum of reindexed copies of $F$, with differentials $d_F$ or $-d_F$ according to the totalization order, hence is acyclic, so the model is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. By [def-weil-derived-tensor] its derived tensor with any degree-zero $k_{V'}$-module sheaf $N$ is therefore the zero-differential complex $\bigoplus_{q=a}^{b-1}N^{\oplus r_q}[-q]$. This has no terms outside $[a,b-1]$. When $a<b$ this proves the required Tor amplitude on every site object, while taking $N=k_{V'}$ gives exactly the constant finite-dimensional cohomology and its stated ranks. Finite sums and shifts here are literal operations on complexes, so the computation uses no preservation-of-completeness under restriction.

source.place: Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat, and Section 06YL (section-flat), tensor total-complex construction; elementary finite split-complex calculation expanding proetale.tex Tag 09C3

proof.text: If $a=b$, the direct sum $W$ is empty, so step 5 gives $L_1=0$. The complete object $L$ of step 3 is zero by [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]. The triangle then makes $f$ an isomorphism by [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero]. If $r_b=0$ and $a<b$, $P=0$, $D=0$, and the cone model in step 5 is simply $W$; thus the construction and amplitude argument also cover that case. If $T$ is empty, all module sheaves and all these maps are zero and the same argument applies.
